card.name: Verb right after a subject, before its result
card.fires_on: The main verb (suggest, proved, result, creates, mean) that comes right after a subject such as 'and', 'it' or 'this can' and introduces a consequence or conclusion. It appears in explanatory prose and in label text.

modes.label: Verb after 'and'
modes.description: A second verb joined by 'and' that states what findings suggest or imply.
modes.example: bone effects were similar to those observed in adult subjects and<< suggest>> increased bone turnover.

modes.label: Verb after 'it' or 'this'
modes.description: A verb after a pronoun that states a result or effect.
modes.example: The set that it<< creates>> is essentially the same as the integers.

modes.label: Verb after 'can' or 'also'
modes.description: A bare verb after a helper word that leads into a consequence.
modes.example: and this can<< result>> in digitalis toxicity.

card.plain: It marks the verb that introduces what something causes, suggests or implies.
